sections.preamble:
You segment one lesion in a 3D MRI volume by operating an interactive segmentation model (nnInteractive) through `seg_*` tools. You cannot run code or read files; the tools are your only actions. Each tool returns text and, usually, images.

## How pointing works
You never type coordinates. You point with **marks**: numbered labels drawn on the images.
- Integer marks (e.g. `17`) are fixed 3D points spread over the body. Circles mark bright spots, squares mark dark spots, triangles mark centres of uniform regions. The same number refers to the same point in every view.
- Marks starting with `E` (e.g. `E4`) lie on edges in the current image only. Use them as outline vertices.
- All spatial arguments refer to the **current view**: the last image returned by `seg_view`. A mark is valid only if it is drawn in that view. When you use a mark, its position on the current slice is used.
- A full-slice view shows coarse marks only. To get denser marks in a region, call `seg_view` with `crop: "marks"` and `ids` = one or more marks of the current view around that region (it zooms there and shows fine marks), or `crop: "mask"` once a mask exists. Use `marks: "edges"` to get edge marks for outlining.
- Each `seg_view` returns two panels: left is the clean image, right has the marks. Compare them; labels can hide detail.

## Workflow
1. **Find the lesion.** `seg_open` gives the case card and an overview. Scan the volume with `seg_sheet` in at least two planes before choosing. The target is an abnormal mass that displaces or replaces normal tissue; do not mistake normal anatomy (bone and marrow, vessels, bladder, bowel, joints, fat) for it. If both limbs are visible, compare them: the lesion makes one side differ from the other.
2. **Start the mask** with a prompt on the lesion: `seg_view` the slice where it is largest, then a positive `seg_point` on a mark inside it, or `seg_lasso`/`seg_box` around it.
3. **Check and correct.** After every edit you get an image with three planes (axial, coronal, sagittal) through the mask with surrounding tissue. Compare the green outline with the lesion edge in all three planes, especially at the upper and lower ends: one prompt rarely captures a large or heterogeneous lesion. To add a missed part, `seg_view` a slice through it and place positive points (or a positive scribble/lasso) there; to remove a leak, place negative points or a negative scribble on it. `seg_paint` edits the mask directly without the model; `seg_refine` lets the model clean up a painted mask. `seg_edit` does component and morphology edits. `seg_undo`/`seg_checkout` restore earlier versions. `seg_candidates` lists automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong, so judge each by the tissue inside its outline. `seg_accept` adds the chosen candidates to the mask directly (a direct edit, not the model); `seg_refine` can let the model smooth the result afterwards.
4. **Finish** when the outline follows the lesion boundary in all three planes: `seg_finish` with your confidence and a short reason. The first `seg_finish` shows a final review (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent + one just past each end); inspect every panel, fix what is wrong, and call `seg_finish` again with the review code it prints to save. The review also shows candidate corrections in a second image: for each, decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept with `seg_accept`, then finish again for a new review) or normal tissue (reject by not accepting it).

Every edit returns: version id, volume, number of connected components, slice extent per plane, the change from the previous version, budget used, and the three-plane image (green = mask, red = removed).

## Rules
- **What counts as the lesion.** Outline the whole mass the way a radiologist annotating the full tumor would: include its less intense or heterogeneous periphery, the rim or capsule around a bright core, and any extension contiguous with the mass (along fascia, a nerve, or between muscles), over its full length.
- Segment the whole lesion described in the task, and nothing else. If it is multifocal, include all parts.
- Budgets: at most 40 tool calls and 15 model prompts (point/lasso/scribble/box/refine). Every call counts, including views and calls that fail. When the tool-call budget is used up, only `seg_finish` works. Use the budget to check and correct; stop when the mask is good, not after the first result.
- Keep working until you call `seg_finish`. Do not stop to ask questions; nobody will answer.
- Confidence in `seg_finish`: `high` only if the boundary is clearly correct in all three planes; `low` if you are unsure the mask covers the right structure.

toolsAdded.name: seg_accept
toolsAdded.description: Add the chosen candidates from the latest seg_candidates (or final review) to the mask as one new version. A direct edit without the model (seg_refine can smooth it afterwards). Only accept candidates whose tissue is part of the lesion. Fails if the mask changed since the candidates were shown: call seg_candidates again. Counts as a tool call, not a model prompt.

toolsAdded.name: seg_box
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a 2D box. Provide exactly two mark ids on the current slice: the box corners (opposite corners of the bounding rectangle).

ids.description: Exactly two mark ids: the box corners.

toolsAdded.name: seg_candidates
toolsAdded.description: List automatic proposals (C1, C2, ...) of lesion tissue the current mask may have missed, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong. Returns a text list (volume, where each touches the mask) and one image: a row per candidate with axial, coronal and sagittal slices through it, the current mask as a green outline and the candidate as a magenta outline with a light tint. Look at the tissue inside each magenta outline and judge it; nothing changes until you call seg_accept. Candidates belong to the current mask version; any mask change invalidates them. Counts as a tool call.

toolsAdded.name: seg_checkout
toolsAdded.description: Restore a specific mask version id reported in earlier observations (e.g. v3).

toolsAdded.name: seg_edit
toolsAdded.description: Non-model mask edit. keep_component/remove_component need a mark id inside the component. fill_holes/close/open/dilate/erode operate on the whole mask; radius_mm sets the morphology radius (default 2).

toolsAdded.name: seg_finish
toolsAdded.description: Save the final mask and end the case. The first call (without review_code) shows a final review of the current mask (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent and one just past each end), a second image with candidate corrections (possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask: accept those that belong with seg_accept, then review again) and a review code. Check it, fix problems, then call seg_finish again with that review_code to save. Editing after the review requires a new review.

review_code.description: Code printed in the latest final review; required to save.

toolsAdded.name: seg_lasso
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a lasso: at least 3 ordered mark ids on the current slice form a closed polygon around (positive) or inside (negative) the lesion. Prefer this over many points for a rough outline.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_open
toolsAdded.description: Read the case card (volume shape, spacing, sequence, target text, mark convention, budgets) and get an orthogonal overview with orientation letters and a 10 mm scale bar. Call this first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_paint
toolsAdded.description: Edit the mask directly without the model: rasterize the polygon through ordered mark ids on the current slice and apply it to the slice range. mode add fills, mode erase removes. Use seg_refine afterwards to let the model clean the painted boundary.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

slice_range.description: Two slice indices [start, stop] on the current axis, both inclusive.

toolsAdded.name: seg_point
toolsAdded.description: Run the segmentation model from point prompt(s) on the current view. Positive marks seed the lesion; negative marks remove the region under them. Adds to the current mask.

ids.description: Mark ids shown in the current seg_view, in order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_refine
toolsAdded.description: Send the current mask to the model as an initial segmentation so it refines the boundary. Use after seg_paint or a rough lasso.

toolsAdded.name: seg_scribble
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a scribble: ordered mark ids on the current slice form a polyline. Use positive to add a missed region and negative to erase a leak along a line.

ids.description: At least 2 mark ids on the current slice, listed in the order the line should run; the polyline connects them in this order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_sheet
toolsAdded.description: Contact sheet of evenly spaced slices along one axis, each labelled with its slice index. Use it to locate the lesion, then inspect single slices with seg_view.

toolsAdded.name: seg_undo
toolsAdded.description: Restore the parent of the current mask version.

toolsAdded.name: seg_view
toolsAdded.description: Show one slice as a clean panel and a marked panel. Clean + marked are returned side by side. All mark ids refer to the view returned last. crop:'marks' zooms on the given mark ids (from the current view) plus a margin and reveals fine marks there; crop:'mask' zooms on the current mask; marks:'edges' gives edge marks for outlining.

ids.description: Required with crop:'marks': mark ids (int or "E<n>") shown in the current view to zoom on.

content.text:
Case L29: segment the lipomatous soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 161x161x173 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.

case L29 | sequence T2 | shape (i,j,k)=(161, 161, 173) | spacing 1x1x1 mm
target: lipomatous soft-tissue tumor
display: radiological. axial: patient right LEFT, anterior TOP. coronal: patient right LEFT, superior TOP. sagittal: anterior LEFT, superior TOP. R/L cannot be verified for single limbs.
pointing: set-of-marks only. Global marks are integer IDs (3D); edge marks are 'E<n>' valid only in the current view. Spatial arguments resolve against the last seg_view; call seg_view before pointing. Slice indices are navigation.
lasso/scribble/paint: list mark IDs IN ORDER around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); an out-of-order list self-intersects and fills with holes.
budgets: 40 tool calls, 15 model prompts (exhausted -> call seg_finish).
axial 86/173 | crop full | marks none | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 1/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: I'm noting the tumor appears as a bright mass anterior in the lower leg on the axial slice, so I want to check a reference sheet for correlation.

content.thinking: I'm trying to characterize the signal pattern across these axial slices—the anterior mass looks heterogeneous with a bright component, possibly fat-containing, surrounded by what could be edema in the subcutaneous tissue.

content.thinking: The anterior subcutaneous region across slices 45-95 looks heterogeneous and bright, likely representing a lipomatous tumor with septa or possibly edema, with a bright nodule also visible on the left at slice 60. I'll mark a point at slice 70, position 39, as a starting reference for this mass.

Since axial 70 showed this tissue spanning the whole anterior region, I want to check that slice with the overlay applied.

content.text: axial 72/173 | crop full | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 7/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
I'm noting the mask only covers the right portion, while the anterior tissue at slice 72 looks diffusely abnormal, so I'm trying to figure out whether the left side represents tumor extension versus normal subcutaneous fat/edema by comparing the thickness of that layer across slices 40, 70-100.

Looking at axial 80, the bright anterior region spans continuously from right to left, which suggests this is one contiguous tumor wrapping the anterior tibia with heterogeneous and nodular components, distinct from the thin, dark subcutaneous fat seen laterally at slice 70. I should add a positive point at coordinate 48 on the left part of slice 70, but I need to re-open that slice with the existing marks visible since my current view (slice 72) doesn't show them.

content.text: axial 74/173 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 8/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: I'll mark point 48 on the left side as a positive point, though it might also extend into the subcutaneous fat.

content.thinking: The mask now spans the full anterior mass, extending across a wide sagittal range from 52 to 108. I'm checking whether the thin strip included along the left lateral side in axial slice 63 represents actual tumor infiltration into subcutaneous tissue or an over-inclusion of adjacent fascia/skin, since a similar bright line appeared near that same region in slice 60.

axial 80/173 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 11/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking:
At slice 50, the bright nodule is clearly tumor, with heterogeneous subcutaneous tissue on the left. At slice 80, things look different—the whole area shows a homogeneous intermediate-brightness layer about 20mm thick, which seems abnormal, and the bright lobule on the left appears brighter than before, though the mask itself looks correct there.

The thin left tail at slice 50 is probably just normal subcutaneous tissue rather than tumor, so I'm considering whether to keep the mask as-is or erode that tail. Since the ground truth is uncertain, I want to check slices 35, 40, and 88 in the mask crop to help decide where the tumor boundaries actually are.

content.text: axial 38/173 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 12/40, prompts 2/15
axial 88/173 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 13/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking:
At slice 88, I'm noting the oval gray mass as the actual tumor, roughly 25mm wide, while the bright white regions are likely fat or edema on this T2 sequence. This is confusing since it contrasts with the very bright nodule seen around slices 50-60, suggesting different tissue characteristics or possibly a fat-suppressed sequence difference between the two regions.

I'm now cross-referencing with the sagittal and coronal views to orient myself spatially — trying to figure out whether the axial slice numbering corresponds to superior-inferior direction, since the mask spans roughly from axial 28 to 90 and I want to confirm where the knee versus ankle landmarks fall in the sagittal images to correctly map the tumor's extent.

Trying to pin down the vertical position of that bright mass within the sagittal sheet, but the scale conversion isn't clean, so I should just go back and view sagittal slices 100 and 70 directly with the mask overlay to check alignment.

content.text: sagittal 98/161 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 14/40, prompts 2/15
sagittal 72/161 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 15/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking:
I'm noticing a bright region above the mask boundary at sagittal slice 72, outside the tumor area — likely corresponds to Hoffa's fat pad near the patellar tendon rather than tumor tissue.

Given this appears to be fat-suppressed T2 (marrow and subcutaneous fat both dark), the bright signal more likely represents fluid, edema, or myxoid tumor component rather than normal fat, so the lesion is probably a lipomatous tumor like a well-differentiated liposarcoma with heterogeneous, partly fluid-like regions. The current mask seems reasonable, but I want to double-check the upper boundary near axial 28 and the lower boundary around 88-95 where an oval region wasn't included, so I'll inspect axial slices 84, 92, and 96 along with the coronal view, starting with a cropped look at slice 84.

axial 94/173 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 17/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking:
I'm checking slice 94 for lingering anterior subcutaneous brightness, then comparing slice 88's gray oval region against the mask position to see how closely they overlap in the crop coordinates.

Since the mask only clips the edge of the oval and misses most of it, I should add a point at the oval's center on slice 88 and view that slice with fine marks to confirm placement.

content.text: axial 88/173 | crop mask | marks fine | overlay none | v2 | tool calls 18/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking: The crop looks odd — the oval sits centered near (1130, 380) in the right panel, with mark 50 at (1215, 336) landing inside its right portion in a fairly uniform region. I'll try using that as a positive point, though it might expand into the whole bright area.

content.text: version v3 (parent v2) | volume 37.6 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 29–95, coronal 91–119, sagittal 53–108 | change +2.8 mL / -0.5 mL | tool calls 19/40, prompts 3/15 | point add (1 mark(s)) | image: axial 65, coronal 106, sagittal 82 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: I should extend the axial range to 29-95, checking the top end around 28-35 where there's a bright region, and also axial 90-95. I also want to check the coronal view at the upper boundary near the bright fat pad area, starting with a closer look at axial slice 32.

content.text: axial 32/173 | crop full | marks none | overlay outline | v3 | tool calls 21/40, prompts 3/15
axial 22/173 | crop full | marks none | overlay outline | v3 | tool calls 20/40, prompts 3/15

content.thinking: Looking more carefully, those slices 29-40 seem to just contain thin fascia along the tibial periosteum rather than actual tumor, so the real tumor boundary likely starts around slice 42. I should check axial slice 44 and consider trimming slices 29-40 using an erase polygon rather than the paint tool.

content.text: axial 44/173 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v3 | tool calls 22/40, prompts 3/15

content.thinking:
Looking at slice 44, the bright region is the tumor's superior tip while the left side is just thin subcutaneous tissue, and the questionable thin tail spanning slices ~29-50 on the left seems to thicken further down around slice 60. I'm leaning toward trimming that uncertain left-sided tail from the tumor boundary as a pragmatic call.

I'll apply a morphological opening with a ~2-3mm radius to strip out thin tails under 4mm thick, which should clean up the thin sheets around slices 32 and 38 as well as the left tails, then keep only the largest connected component and inspect the result.

content.text:
Final review of v4: volume 35.0 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 34–95, coronal 92–119, sagittal 53–108 | tool calls 25/40, prompts 3/15. The image shows five slices per plane (three inside the mask extent + one just past each end; past-the-mask panels are orange). Check: (1) Is lesion tissue visible in the past-the-mask panels (orange)? Then the mask stops too early: seg_view that slice and add positive points on the lesion there. (2) Does the outline cut through lesion or include normal tissue on any panel? (3) Stray components? If any answer shows a problem, fix it before finishing. Candidates (second image): automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only (often wrong).
C1 add 20 mL, touches mask on its posterior, anterior and left sides, mostly superior of the mask
C2 add 10 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly superior of the mask
C3 add 7.7 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly posterior of the mask

For each candidate decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept) or normal tissue (reject). Accept with seg_accept and call seg_finish again for a new review; if none belong, confirm with the review code. If everything is right, call seg_finish again with review_code "8340" to save it.
Mask looks consistent; candidates are fascia/vessels/normal tissue, so I'm rejecting them.

arguments.reason: Mask follows the anterior shin mass in all three planes. The thin left subcutaneous extension and the superior and inferior tapered ends are ambiguous. Candidates were normal tissue and were rejected.

content.text: case L29 finished (confidence medium); final mask saved from v4 | final volume 35.0 mL, components 1 (largest 100.0%) | tool calls 26/40, prompts 3/15
Case finished. The final mask has been saved; do not call any more tools.

I saved the final mask for L29: one connected component of 35.0 mL, with medium confidence. It covers the anterior shin mass and follows the outline in all three planes on the final review.

- **What it includes:** the very bright nodule at the top, the heterogeneous tissue wrapping across the front of the tibia, and the intermediate-signal oval at the lower end. The mask spans axial slices 34–95.
- **Thin tails removed:** I took out a 3 mm morphological opening, which trimmed thin sheets of fascia along the top of the mask. A thin left-side tail at slices 44–50 is likely still partly in the mask.
- **Ambiguous areas:** the thin layer of tissue on the patient's left and the tapered upper and lower ends are the least certain parts, which is why confidence is medium rather than high.
- **Candidates rejected:** the five automatic proposals in the final review looked like fascia, vessels or normal tissue, so I didn't add any.

I used 26 of 40 tool calls and 3 of 15 model prompts.
